Project Name: Automated Account Registration & Ticket Generation System
Problem: Manual account creation and ticket submission across multiple external platforms is repetitive, time-consuming, and not scalable for support operations
Solution: Developed a Selenium-based automation engine that executes end-to-end workflows including account registration, login, navigation, and ticket submission using structured input datasets
Architecture Overview: Input-driven automation pipeline where URLs and user data are parsed from files and executed sequentially through a browser automation engine with dynamic page handling
Architecture Components: Workflow Executor (Register -> Login -> Navigate -> Submit Ticket)
Data Flow: Load target URLs from input file
Navigate to support or help section
Persist execution results to output log
Core Features: End-to-end workflow execution (registration to ticket submission)
Duplicate prevention and controlled execution rate
Input and Output: output.txt (execution logs with credentials and ticket details)
Metrics: Stable execution across repeated batch runs
Multi-site processing with consistent success tracking
Per-run logging of success and failure states
Testing Scenarios: Execution across websites with varying DOM structures
Repeated user registration and ticket submission
Handling missing fields and unexpected page layouts
Testing Results: Reliable detection of input fields across multiple platforms
Challenges: Handling variability in website structures and navigation flows
Preventing duplicate registrations and repeated submissions
Challenge Solutions: Implemented dynamic element detection instead of static selectors
Introduced validation, tracking, and rate limiting mechanisms
Designed fallback handling strategies for CAPTCHA interruptions
Engineering Focus: Designing a reusable automation engine rather than a one-off script
Handling real-world variability in web interfaces
Proof Status: Validated through large-scale execution logs and repeated batch runs
